report.summary: The only failure is test_invalid_book_is_rejected[blank-title], which expected a whitespace-only title to be rejected with 422 but got 201. The app code has the seeded blank_title bug: validate_book skips the blank-title check when BUGS contains blank_title. Fix first by confirming whether BUGS=blank_title is set on the CI runner; the workflow does not set it, so an unintended leaked env var would make this a configuration problem rather than a product fix.

causes.title: Whitespace-only book title is accepted when the blank_title seeded bug is active
causes.explanation: validate_book only rejects a blank title when "blank_title" is not in BUGS, so with that flag set a title of "   " passes validation and the API returns 201 Created. The test's expectation of 422 matches the intended validation rule (the message 'Title must not be blank'), so the test is right and the app is wrong. The other three parametrizations of the same test passed, which fits a single defect being switched on; the year_off_by_one bug would have failed the next-year case, and it did not. The one open question is where BUGS=blank_title comes from: the workflow in .github/workflows/tests.yml does not set it, and the conftest passes the inherited environment through to uvicorn. If the flag was not meant to be on in CI, this is an infrastructure/config problem and the fix is to remove the variable.
evidence: app/main.py:10: blank_title      accepts a title made only of spaces
app/main.py:86: if not book.title.strip() and "blank_title" not in BUGS:
app/main.py:87: raise HTTPException(422, "Title must not be blank")
app/main.py:31: BUGS = {b.strip() for b in os.environ.get("BUGS", "").split(",") if b.strip()}
tests/conftest.py:57: env = {**os.environ, "DB_PATH": db_path}  (the app subprocess inherits BUGS from the runner environment)
.github/workflows/tests.yml:35: pytest -m ${{ matrix.suite }} -n auto ... (no BUGS variable set in the workflow)
causes.suggested_fix: Confirm the runner environment: check whether BUGS=blank_title is set on the CI machine or in the job. If the bug is meant to be seeded for this run, mark this test as expected-fail (xfail) or leave it as a deliberate finding. If not, unset BUGS so the app runs with correct validation. Do not change the test, since its expectation is correct. Optionally, make the app read BUGS only when an explicit opt-in flag is set so a stray variable cannot change behavior silently.
